assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of quantum matter in which bulk topology forces protected boundary states. The theoretical prediction, the HgTe quantum spin Hall realization and the three-dimensional ARPES identification form a clear chain from idea to observed phenomenon, and the concept has spread into photonics, superconductivity and materials discovery. The discovery is central, original and lastingly influential.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the decisive Z2 theory; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental quantum spin Hall realization in HgTe wells (building on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not among the credited names); Hasan's group identified the first 3D topological insulators experimentally. Mele is a real co-originator of the Z2 classification but a three-person limit forces a choice, and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Moore-Balents/Fu-Kane-Mele theory credit is only partly representable. I propose the theory leader and the two experimental pioneers.
assessment.maturity: Strongly and independently confirmed across many materials and techniques over roughly two decades; the interpretation is stable. The 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and topological phases in a related but distinct sense, so recognition of this specific discovery is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: How the committee weighs the 2016 prize overlap and whether Mele or a BHZ author should displace one of the three proposed names.
I rely on recalled history for exact priority among the 2005-2008 theory and experiment papers and have not verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the subsequent source associations (the 2017 blazar TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, and the Galactic plane) established neutrino astronomy as a working field. A discovery with a clear observable, a clear instrument and broad implications for cosmic-ray origins, which is the type of discovery-centred case I favour.
assessment.attribution: Only Halzen is credited, so this configuration is a single laureate. He is widely recognised as the originator and long-time leader of IceCube, but the discovery is the product of a large collaboration and the credited list cannot represent other key contributors (for example in detector design and analysis); the committee would have to resolve who else could be named, and a single-name prize may under-represent the effort.
assessment.maturity: Strong: the astrophysical flux has been confirmed by multiple analyses and channels, with the source identifications adding independent support. Source-level interpretations are still evolving, but the discovery of the flux itself is stable and mature enough for recognition now.
uncertainties: Fairness of a single-name configuration for a large collaboration result.
Source-population interpretation remains incomplete, though the discovery itself does not depend on it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation resolved the horizon and flatness problems and, through quantum fluctuations seeding structure, made a quantitative prediction later confirmed in CMB anisotropies. Its conceptual impact on cosmology and early-universe physics is very large and it is a foundational framework connecting quantum field theory to observation.
assessment.attribution: Credit is notoriously entangled: Guth's 1981 proposal, Linde's new/chaotic inflation, Starobinsky's earlier model and the fluctuation calculations by Mukhanov and Chibisov, Hawking, Starobinsky, Guth-Pi and Bardeen-Steinhardt-Turner. Among the credited names, Guth, Linde and Mukhanov cover the idea, the viable scenario and the structure-formation link, but Starobinsky, Albrecht and Steinhardt and others cannot be represented, so the allocation is genuinely unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The CMB acoustic peaks, near scale-invariant adiabatic spectrum and flatness strongly support the inflationary paradigm, but the specific inflaton dynamics are unconstrained and primordial gravitational waves have not been detected. The paradigm is mature enough in its observational support, though a strict reading of confirmation would call it incomplete.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial B-modes; competing early-universe scenarios are not fully excluded.
Attribution among many originators; the credited trio omits recognised contributors.
As a theorist in adjacent fields I may be inclined to favour conceptual cosmology; I weight the observational confirmation separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, combines the stability of many neutral atoms with optical frequencies and has pushed fractional uncertainties to the 1e-18 level. It enables tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second, making it an original, measurable and widely used advance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated the first clocks; Ye's group drove the clock to extreme precision and carried out tests of systematic effects and many-body physics. Both names are credited and the two-person configuration is coherent. Contributions from others in the field (for example Hall and Hänsch frequency-comb work, already recognised in 2005) are separate.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced across many laboratories worldwide; the technology is mature, with international comparisons and a roadmap towards redefinition of the second. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier precision-measurement prizes and with ion-clock work by others not credited here.
The precise division of credit between theory proposal and ultimate performance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localisation of gamma-ray bursts by BeppoSAX and the discovery of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows settled the long-standing cosmological-distance debate and tied bursts to extreme stellar collapse and relativistic fireballs. A decisive observational discovery that reshaped high-energy astrophysics and later linked to supernovae and compact-object mergers.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX instrument and the rapid localisation that led to the first X-ray afterglow; Kulkarni's group led the optical/radio follow-up and redshift identification. The chain from instrument team to follow-up observers is clear, though others (for example van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Metzger and the Wide Field Camera team) are not credited and the best three-person allocation is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the cosmological origin has been confirmed for nearly three decades, with extensive later confirmation including the GW170817 association. Timely in principle, possibly overdue.
uncertainties: Competing credit among the optical-identification groups not on this list.
Whether the committee views this as sufficiently within physics, as opposed to astronomy, for the physics prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices provide clean, tunable realisations of Hubbard-type many-body models, beginning with the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and now including quantum gas microscopy. The idea of quantum simulation joined to a concrete implementation has substantially influenced condensed-matter and quantum-information physics.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard implementation (Jaksch is not credited) and Zoller is credited as a theory leader; Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott transition and developed the microscopy. Esslinger (fermionic Hubbard) and Cirac are also credited, so any three-person configuration leaves out strongly deserving contributors.
assessment.maturity: Well established and independently reproduced; the field is mature in techniques, although useful quantum advantage in simulation of open problems is still emerging.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with other quantum-simulation platforms credited elsewhere.
Choice among five credited names is difficult and partly subjective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Halperin-Nelson-Young theory of defect-mediated two-dimensional melting, with a hexatic intermediate phase and two continuous transitions, extended the Kosterlitz-Thouless idea to a second broad class of phase transitions. The prediction is conceptually elegant, general and has been tested in colloids, liquid crystals and numerical simulations.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson formulated the theory, and Young produced the closely related independent result and numerical support. The credited trio matches the standard KTHNY attribution; Kosterlitz and Thouless were already honoured in 2016, so this would complete the story. Allocation of credit within the trio seems relatively straightforward.
assessment.maturity: Predictions were established decades ago and tested in multiple experimental systems; the interpretation is stable though real 2D melting scenarios remain somewhat system-dependent. Recognition is arguably late rather than premature, but the added novelty relative to 2016 may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers the 2016 prize to have sufficiently covered this territory.
System-dependent first-order versus continuous melting scenarios in experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of the baryon acoustic feature in galaxy clustering provides a standard ruler that anchors cosmological distance measurements and constrains dark energy. It is a clear, observationally decisive discovery whose impact has grown through subsequent surveys and was predicted by well-understood early-universe physics.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein et al. (SDSS) and Cole et al. (2dFGRS) reported nearly simultaneous independent detections in 2005; Percival is credited for subsequent analysis but the decisive original detections are best linked to the two teams' lead analysts. Theory origins of the acoustic-scale idea (Peebles-Yu, Sunyaev-Zeldovich and others) are not represented.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by multiple surveys, with increasingly precise results from BOSS and DESI, though dark-energy interpretation continues to evolve.
uncertainties: Attribution to survey leads versus the theory originators and to large collaborations.
Possible overlap with prizes already awarded for cosmic acceleration and CMB work.
